executiveSummary: GM0556 passes the complete deterministic execution contract across all ten canonical presets, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its 2025 CBS/PDOK identity, generalized boundary, 36,436 residents, 19 neighbourhoods, one BAG place, one BRT woonkern and Rotterdam-Rijnmond safety-region assignment reconcile. Release remains correction-required. The generated municipality has zero logical transport links despite the CC0 NWB A20 corridor crossing it and 29 GTFS stop areas including metro context. Eight unrelated non-earthquake single-hazard presets reuse exactly the same complete T+24 neighbourhood order; even river and coastal flooding rank the waterfront neighbourhood Nieuwe waterweg only ninth. The river preset exposes 2.04095 metres of local 'flood depth' unchanged from T+12 through T+72, while the coastal preset exposes 1.87653 metres at T+24, but neither is bound to a selected Nieuwe Waterweg water-level series, tidal/rhine discharge combination, outer/inner harbour split, primary/secondary defence state or Maeslantkering state. Official Maassluis evidence instead distinguishes water level relative to NAP from local inundation depth, four forecast-triggered outer-harbour action phases, and a separate extreme-rain inner-harbour pathway. One current Waterinfo observation and forecasts only through T+48 are valuable time-stamped context, not calibration for a canonical event or T+72 state. Active Kortebuurt defence work, 60 public water assets, external acute care, air quality, utilities and first-72-hour actions remain absent from the causal model. Unknown and NoData must not be converted to zero, safety, passability, capacity or recovery.

evidenceSources.title: Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025 — filtered rows for GM0556
supports: Official GM0556/Maassluis identity, population 36,436, density 4,315 residents per square kilometre, 22.8% aged 65 or older and 5,584 one-person households.
The annual machine-readable OData release is CC BY 4.0. Neighbourhood values are rounded and some fields are suppressed or not applicable; null, Unknown and NoData must never become zero.

CBS supports transparent aggregate demand and vulnerability context, not named vulnerable people, institutional occupants, event-time commuters, household emergency stocks, observed customers or casualties.

evidenceSources.publisher: PDOK / CBS / Kadaster / Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi
evidenceSources.title: Generalized areas 2025 with BAG, BRT TOP10NL, NWB, rail and public-transport context
supports: The application consumes the 2025 CC BY 4.0 generalized municipality and 19-neighbourhood geometry. Reference point [4.252811358931954, 51.92212986714131] and the one BAG place centre are inside GM0556.
BAG woonplaatsen are Public Domain Mark 1.0 at https://api.pdok.nl/kadaster/bag/ogc/v2/collections/woonplaats. BRT TOP10NL is CC BY 4.0 with rotating updates and retains Maassluis as one woonkern.

Monthly CC0 NWB geometry is downloadable at https://downloads.rijkswaterstaatdata.nl/nwb-wegen/geogegevens/shapefile/NWB-light/01-08-2026.zip. Its aggregated ##020/A20 line runs through the Maassluis extent, yet the generated logical graph contains zero GM0556 edges or neighbours.

ProRail OGC is CC0 static infrastructure context; zero ProRail stations is expected for the converted line but is not zero public transport. Twenty-nine GTFS stop areas include Maassluis Centrum, Maassluis West and Steendijkpolder/metro-labelled context; schedules and stop points do not prove incident operation or capacity.

evidenceSources.title: Hoogwater page, Action plan high water unembanked Maassluis area v1.1, and Ramp or crisis guidance
evidenceSources.edition: Web page modified 21 April 2026; action plan v1.1 definitive May 2021; crisis page modified 23 June 2026
supports: The harbour is openly connected to the Nieuwe Waterweg. After the keersluis in the Delflandsedijk closes, the outer harbour remains connected and can flood; the inner harbour is then separated from the Nieuwe Waterweg but can rise during extreme rain. The 2021 action plan expressly excludes inner-harbour rain measures.

Nieuwe Waterweg high water combines tide and river discharge; the peak arrives in Maassluis about 45 minutes after Hoek van Holland. The action plan records at least 12 hours' WMCN notification before the expected NAP +2.00 m pre-warning level, but forecast and actual peaks can differ.

Four outer-harbour phases use forecast water level, not local flood depth: NAP +2.00–2.20, +2.20–2.80, +2.80–3.10 and above +3.10 m. Named consequences include Burgemeester De Jonghkade, Govert van Wijnkade, the Nieuwe Waterweg business-area stormwater system from +2.70, the boulevard cycleway/ferry landing from +2.90 and residential 't Hoofd above +3.10.

Named actions include notifying municipal operations, police, Delfland, harbour businesses and resident contacts, publishing warnings, closing the loswal/barriers and warning vehicle/vessel owners. These are plan tasks, not evidence that an action is currently triggered, resourced or complete.

The current crisis page directs shelter-in-place, ventilation shutdown, NL-Alert/Rijnmondveilig information, police-directed evacuation and institutional transport for people needing assistance. It also notes regional production, storage and transport of dangerous substances. No blanket machine-data licence or fixed update cadence was established; the older action-plan roles and contacts require operational revalidation.

evidenceSources.title: Maeslantkering operation and public Waterinfo Maassluis observation/forecast point
evidenceSources.edition: Maeslantkering page modified 22 May 2026; Waterinfo observation retrieved 2 September 2026 and forecasts 3 September 2026
supports: The automated Maeslantkering is a forward defence against sea high water and forms the Europoortkering with the Hartelkering and Rozenburg dike widening. The official closure levels are a forecast NAP +3.0 m at Rotterdam or +2.9 m at Dordrecht; RWS says it can withstand a 5 m NAP surge and experts monitor expected closures.

Closure protects against sea surge but does not erase upstream river discharge, inner-system rainfall, local defence or unembanked exposure. Maintenance/testing and a closure threshold are not an event-time reliability guarantee or local depth surface.

The CC0 Waterinfo snapshot contains one Maassluis observation: 122 cm NAP at 2026-09-02T17:30Z, classified normal and fresh at retrieval. It is a point water level, not local inundation depth, breach, probability or defence state.

Rolling public forecasts return Maassluis values through T+48: 127, 5, 51, 25 and 6 cm NAP at requested T+1/+6/+12/+24/+48 windows. No T+72 point is returned. Coverage declines by horizon; the public frontend JSON is not documented as a stable external API, and empty T+72 is NoData rather than zero water.

Observation, issued forecast, historical replay, official scenario and canonical deterministic forcing are different evidence classes and must retain retrieval, issue/valid time, station/datum, quality flag and licence.

evidenceSources.title: Public Hoogwaterkaart Rotterdam web application referenced by Maassluis
evidenceSources.edition: Application modified 23 June 2025; linked web map inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The public application is explicitly linked by Maassluis for address-and-expected-water-level exploration and identifies Gemeente Rotterdam/Rijkswaterstaat provenance and CC BY 4.0 reuse.

Its own description says the map concerns unembanked area, does not state flood probability and is indicative; reality can differ through wind, waves and backwater. The app must not be treated as observed flood depth or guaranteed protection.

The linked web map exposes queryable high-water polygons, AHN terrain, defences and water-level sites through ArcGIS services. Before simulation use, province review must verify GM0556 spatial coverage, source date, threshold units, vertical datum, resolution and NoData rather than inheriting the application's Rotterdam-labelled extent.

evidenceSources.title: Kortebuurt Maassluis dike strengthening and public water-control/wastewater objects
evidenceSources.edition: Project page last modified 18 November 2025; HWH deployment snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: Delfland says parts of the Kortebuurt dike are too low or insufficiently robust, the current embankment is in poor condition and extra measures are being taken while a nature permit is awaited. Planned phases include damming a Boonervliet branch with a closable culvert to limit inflow after breach, berms and later raising. Planned/completed work is not live defence state.

The deployed partial HWH CC BY-SA 4.0 snapshot intersects 60 GM0556 features: two sewer pumps, ten surface-water pumps, four sluices and 44 weirs. Fifty capacities are null; geometry/status labels do not establish hydraulic connectivity, setpoint, telemetry, backup or restoration.

Named objects include Rg Maassluis, Rg Merellaan, Dijkpolder/Wilgenrijk and Foppenpolder Zuid pumps, Wateringsesluis, Monstersche Sluis, Keersluis Maassluis and Deltakering Boonerhaven. Contributor-dependent coverage and record presence are static context, not proof of complete assets or operation.

evidenceSources.publisher: RIVM / DCMR / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / NDW
evidenceSources.title: Acute care, indicative air quality, grid planning, telecom, education and road situations
evidenceSources.edition: RIVM acute-care questionnaire 2026 v1.1; deployment snapshots inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The versioned national RIVM acute-care questionnaire is CC0 and has no hospital point inside GM0556. Straight-line reference-point distances are about 8.72 km to non-24/7 Franciscus Vlietland in Schiedam and 10.20 km to 24/7 Reinier de Graaf in Delft; distances and reported roles/rooms/2025 visits are not ambulance travel, acceptance, staffing, occupancy or backup.

DCMR station Maassluis-Kwartellaan reported indicative PM2.5 2.6 micrograms per cubic metre for 2026-09-02T16:00–17:00Z. Luchtmeetnet measurements can be revised and have no standard reuse licence stated; one hourly point is not a smoke plume, exposure surface, source attribution or forecast.

The one NBNL postcode sample 3142NX assigns Stedin area Maassluis 1 but reports null existing/required capacity, zero queued values and no projects. The product is planning context from public frontend JSON with exact licence/stability unstated; null and sampled zero do not mean zero capacity, no grid risk, live state or restoration.

The deployed context contains 34 RDI sites and 19 DUO locations but no GM0556 government-service, weather-observation/warning/seismic or NDW situation record. Antennas and schools do not establish coverage, backup, shelter or distribution roles; empty current feeds are coverage NoData, not safety, open roads or future state.

geography.summary: The reference point lies inside the generalized municipality, but high-water modelling needs explicit unembanked/embanked, harbour, defence and cross-boundary water geometry.

The Nieuwe Waterweg, Maeslantkering, tide/river boundary conditions, Delflandsedijk/keersluis, unembanked harbour and Delfland polder/boezem systems cross municipal and authority boundaries.
Generalized geometry cannot establish local water level/depth, defence state, stormwater/sewer connectivity, pump/sluice control, route passability or asset ownership.

regionalDetail.summary: All 19 neighbourhoods load, but missing attributes and public assets/observations retain source-specific coverage and non-causal semantics.

The Nieuwe waterweg neighbourhood has only 105 published residents but 145 non-residential buildings and 110 businesses, showing why population alone cannot allocate harbour operational exposure.
Water objects, Waterinfo, PM2.5, grid-planning, antennas, schools and care sites are typed context. They cannot be promoted to live topology, observed consequence, capacity or T+72 state.

settlements.summary: One BAG woonplaats and one BRT woonkern named Maassluis are retained without a boundary mismatch.
notes: The municipality has one BAG woonplaats and BRT settlement label, both Maassluis.
The 19 neighbourhoods preserve waterfront, polder, old-centre and residential labels needed for aggregation.
Administrative/topographic labels do not establish event-time population, isolation, refuge capacity or service availability.

transport.summary: The logical graph isolates Maassluis despite A20 geometry and metro/ferry/urban-road dependencies.
notes: logicalRouteDegree is zero: there are no neighbours, route names, service links or inbound/outbound transfer edges for any hazard.

The deployed monthly NWB layer contains the ##020/A20 corridor across the Maassluis extent. Twenty-nine GTFS areas include metro-labelled stations, and the action plan identifies a ferry landing that begins flooding from NAP +2.90 m.
No graph path represents Vlaardingen/Schiedam/Rotterdam, Midden-Delfland/Westland, A20, metro, ferry, harbour access, bridge/barrier closure or route-dependent external care.
Zero NDW situations is a deployment-time empty assignment, not proof every road is open and never a forecast to T+72.

emergencyContext.summary: Official four-phase high-water tasks exist, but no trigger, action, resource, facility, evacuation or household-readiness state enters the simulation.
notes: The public action plan ties outer-harbour consequences and named municipal/police/Delfland communications and closures to forecast NAP thresholds, with WMCN warning context about 12 hours before +2.00 m.
The model has no issued forecast binding, threshold transition, action owner, requested/confirmed/completed state, resource constraint, expiry or result.

Crisis guidance, school/institutional transport and shelter-in-place are instructions or plan roles, not automatically completed actions. Household supplies and ability to receive SMS/NL-Alert remain Unknown.
Zero local acute hospitals and external questionnaire records do not establish route access, ambulance time, acceptance, occupancy, staffing, generator/fuel or continuity.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets produce complete finite deterministic outputs at six checkpoints and eight services; physical and evidence contradictions are recorded separately.
notes: The focused gate executed severe storm, pluvial flood, river flood, coastal flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

Maximum severity / maximum affected people-equivalent / T+72 cumulative local pre-network event-attributable person-hours are storm 0.327252 / 5,994 / 290,135.719; pluvial 0.515986 / 12,305 / 474,169.410; river 0.637333 / 23,340 / 1,293,988.661; coastal 0.583452 / 22,256 / 1,187,399.919; heat 0.564006 / 2,313 / 225,347.600.
These are exercise outputs, not measurements, probabilities, warnings, casualties, identified customers, damage assessments or restoration forecasts.

numericalInvariants.summary: The focused gate passes deterministic, finite, exact-zero, causal, allocation, reconciliation and monotonic-burden contracts.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0556 pnpm audit:model passed both tests on current code across 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services.
Every intensity-zero run has exactly zero event severity, affected people-equivalent and event-attributable deprived person-hours; repeated output and web/core preset parity pass.
All local rows allocate exactly 36,436 residents and service demand/delivery totals reconcile within floating-point tolerance.
Selected display service creates zero local-hazard delta, cumulative event-attributable person-hours are monotonic and declared logical-route ceilings hold vacuously for the zero-edge graph.

spatialPlausibility.summary: A shared neighbourhood ordering cannot represent outer-harbour high water, pluvial drainage, heat, winter, cyber, smoke and other local mechanisms.
notes: At T+24 storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and canonical wildfire have exactly the same complete 19-neighbourhood order: Steendijkpolder Zuid, Vertobuurt, Taanschuurpolder, Binnenstad and Burgemeesterswijk lead.

The waterfront Nieuwe waterweg neighbourhood ranks ninth for every one of those presets despite E03's phase-specific outer-harbour sites and its 145 non-residential buildings. Compound differs mainly through saturation; earthquake has a zero-hazard baseline order.

No official outer-harbour contour, high-water map, current Waterinfo boundary, Delfland rain/asset system, valid-time weather/air field, cyber target or selected ground-motion grid controls local allocation.
Canonical wildfire has zero local direct fire and only smoke/drought. That is a remote-source scenario result, not evidence that urban/industrial or nature fire is impossible.

serviceDependencies.summary: Eight service scores remain precise even though Maassluis has no logical network edge and no validated physical lifeline topology.
notes: The city-detail graph has links=[] and therefore represents no intermunicipal mobility, logistics, care or utility transfer; each service still reports an exact synthetic Maassluis gateway and restoration path.

At compound T+24 availability is power 0.439922, water 0.333193, drainage 0.213601, gas 0.576094, telecom 0.259668, mobility 0.373562, facilities 0.482933 and supply 0.309384. At T+72 facilities alone worsens to 0.316619 while all other values remain exactly fixed.

HWH objects, one NBNL sample, antenna/school points and external hospital records are contextual. They do not establish feeder, pipe, sewer, pump/sluice, backhaul, route, customer load, backup, stock, priority, crew or restoration state.
Drinking-water quantity/quality, wastewater, stormwater, surface-water control, marine/river level and flood defence are distinct systems and cannot safely collapse into water and drainage scores.

causalTrace.summary: Stage arithmetic closes, but metres of flood depth are not tied to NAP water level, inundation footprint or defence state and are operationally misleading.
notes: River forcing reaches 2.040950 m flood depth at T+12 and remains exactly unchanged through T+72; affected rises from 19,959 to 23,340 and person-hours to 1,293,988.661. No selected Rhine discharge/tide series, local level-depth transform, defence or footprint supports it.

Coastal T+24 exposes 1.876526 m depth, 22,256 affected and 0.573542 pressure; direct depth is zero at T+72 but 4,447 remain affected and person-hours reach 1,187,399.919. No Maeslantkering/keersluis state or action explains the transition.

Official thresholds are water surface elevation relative to NAP and local contour consequences; simulated floodDepthM denotes local depth. These quantities cannot be compared or substituted without terrain/datum and connected inundation logic.
Current point observation/forecast, older action plan, active dike project, official indicative map and synthetic scenario remain separate evidence classes.

recovery72h.summary: The first-72-hour trajectories ignore published trigger actions, current forecast coverage limits, transport isolation, facility state and operator restoration evidence.
notes: The river scenario is a complete plateau from T+12 through T+72 for hazard depth and seven services, with facilities degrading later; no selected event, tide, defence, closure, repair or response explains that persistence.
Current Waterinfo data supports Maassluis only through requested T+48; no T+72 record exists. Forecast gaps cannot be filled with zero or canonical exercise values.

Compound severity declines to 0.602236 at T+72 while affected increases to 25,896, pressure reaches 0.644458 and seven service values are frozen from T+24; no recorded intervention or resource state explains the curve.

No WMCN alert receipt, barrier/loswal/keersluis closure, resident/business message, vehicle movement, evacuation, pump/sluice operation, hospital acceptance, utility switching, crew/fuel/spares, household stock or action completion drives the result. Seventy-two hours is a preparedness horizon, not a recovery promise.

findings.summary: River and coastal presets expose unsupported metre-precision without a Nieuwe Waterweg boundary, defence state or level-to-depth transform.
findings.evidence: River floodDepthM is exactly 2.040950 from T+12 through T+72; coastal is 1.876526 at T+24. E03 defines a different physical contract: water level in metres NAP, tide plus river discharge, an outer/inner harbour split, a 45-minute Hoek van Holland lag and four consequence contours. E04 adds Maeslantkering closure semantics and a current level series. No selected boundary event, local terrain/depth surface, defence/keersluis state, failure mode, arrival/recession or uncertainty supports the outputs.
findings.action: Build one Nieuwe Waterweg compound boundary adapter with explicit tide, surge and upstream discharge components, then derive separate local surface elevation/depth footprints for embanked and unembanked areas. Keep river and coastal views as decompositions of the same selected event, preserve datum/units/defence state/validity/uncertainty/NoData and never equate NAP elevation with flood depth.

findings.summary: The simulator omits Maassluis's public four-phase high-water triggers and first-72-hour action ledger.
findings.evidence: E03 defines action phases at expected NAP +2.00–2.20, +2.20–2.80, +2.80–3.10 and above +3.10 m, WMCN notification context at least 12 hours before +2.00 m, affected locations and named municipal/police/Delfland communications and closures. The model records none of the alert, owner, action, resource, status or outcome fields and instead advances exact service/recovery values. The plan is v1.1 May 2021 even though still linked from a page updated April 2026, so operational confirmation is required.
findings.action: Ingest a municipality-authorized current phase/action table. Track proposed/requested/confirmed/completed/cancelled tasks with trigger, owner, source, issued/valid/expiry time, resource need, dependency, confidence and outcome. Do not infer completion from the model clock or a forecast threshold alone.

findings.summary: Maassluis is an isolated zero-edge node despite A20, metro, ferry and external-care dependencies.
findings.evidence: audit:context reports logicalRouteDegree 0, no neighbours and no routes. E02's deployed CC0 NWB layer contains the A20/##020 corridor across the municipal extent and 29 GTFS areas include metro-labelled stops. E03 says the ferry landing floods from NAP +2.90 m. E07 places the nearest listed acute care outside the municipality. Static geometry does not prove operation, but zero topology is a reproducible omission.
findings.action: Generate audited A20/local-road, metro, ferry/harbour and route-dependent care/logistics edges with authority, mode, direction, topology semantics and non-additive capacity. Apply event-valid NDW/operator/municipal restrictions separately; Unknown current state never means open.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated hazard presets reuse one neighbourhood rank and under-specify the official waterfront mechanism.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire share exactly the same full T+24 order, led by Steendijkpolder Zuid. Nieuwe waterweg ranks ninth even though E03 names its business-area drainage and adjacent harbour sites in threshold consequences and the CBS row contains 145 non-residential buildings. No selected official contour, high-water map, rain/depth, weather, cyber-target, smoke or seismic surface drives the order.
findings.action: Replace the shared seed with mechanism-specific, coverage-aware fields and explicitly mark unsupported layers. Preserve source geometry, CRS, vertical datum, units, edition, issue/valid time, resolution, licence and NoData. Test that selected outer-harbour high-water contours drive the appropriate waterfront cells without using population alone.

findings.summary: Extreme-rain inner-harbour, stormwater, sewer and Delfland polder mechanisms are absent from the pluvial output.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports 0.714442 m depth, 12,305 affected and drainage availability 0.378191 without a source-native depth/flow surface. E03 explicitly says the closed inner harbour can rise during extreme rain and that its action plan excludes those measures; from NAP +2.70 the business-area stormwater system can also become submerged. E06 supplies 60 partial water objects, but 50 capacities are null and none is connected or live.
findings.action: Create a separate pluvial/inner-water pathway using a selected rainfall hyetograph, terrain/imperviousness, municipal sewer/stormwater, Delfland polder/boezem, pump/sluice and receiving-water boundary data. Preserve source coverage/NoData and keep static register objects non-causal until connectivity, capacity and state are authorized.

findings.summary: Active local defence condition and planned works are not represented and cannot be assumed complete.
findings.evidence: E06 says Kortebuurt is in poor condition, locally too low or insufficiently robust, has extra interim measures and awaits a nature permit; planned work includes a closable-culvert dam to limit Boonervliet inflow after a breach. E03/E04 identify the local keersluis and Maeslantkering. The model exposes no defence reach, owner, edition, inspection/works state, closure threshold, reliability or failure mode.
findings.action: Add a time-stamped, authority-reviewed defence layer with reach, owner, function, condition/works state, threshold, actual closure and failure/uncertainty semantics. Planned, under-construction and operational states remain distinct; never infer protection from an asset point or project page.

findings.summary: Exact service trajectories have neither physical topology nor event-authorized operator evidence.
findings.evidence: With links=[], compound T+24 availability ranges from drainage 0.213601 to gas 0.576094 and seven services remain exactly unchanged through T+72 while facilities worsens. E06/E07 provide water objects, a null-heavy one-postcode grid sample, antennas, schools and external hospitals only. No source validates physical feeders/pipes/sewers/backhaul, dependency direction, backup, stock, switching, crew or restoration.
findings.action: Give each service explicit topologySemantics/evidence/version/coverage fields. Use only security-reviewed operator or authority state; otherwise keep physical topology and live availability Unknown or use the smallest transparently aggregate synthetic exercise fallback. NWB/GTFS may support mobility and assumed logistics only.

findings.summary: Current Maassluis Waterinfo data ends at T+48 and must not be blended into the canonical T+72 scenario.
findings.evidence: E04 records one observation and station forecasts at requested +1/+6/+12/+24/+48 windows, all in cm NAP, but no +72 record. The simulator river and coastal outputs run to T+72 without referencing station, issue/valid time or datum. Current normal classification is only for the retrieved observation and cannot certify later safety or a synthetic event.
findings.action: Add a governed current-data mode that binds station, issue/valid time, horizon, datum, quality and stale/NoData status. Stop or mark Unknown beyond the source forecast horizon; keep canonical exercises and historical replays separate and never fill missing T+72 with zero.

findings.summary: External care, assisted evacuation, shelter/communications and industrial continuity remain Unknown.
findings.evidence: There is no acute-hospital point in GM0556. The nearest questionnaire locations are about 8.72 km straight-line to non-24/7 Franciscus Vlietland and 10.20 km to 24/7 Reinier de Graaf, which are not incident travel or acceptance. E03 assigns special transport to institutions and identifies dangerous-substance activity; E07 contributes 34 antennas and 19 schools but no live capability. The simulator has no route, staff, occupancy, backup, reception, distribution, ventilation or assisted-transport state.
findings.action: Separate time-dependent route/ambulance reachability from facility capability and industrial/shelter-in-place actions. Accept only event-authorized municipality, GHOR, facility, operator and school states with owner, validity, expiry and confidence; all other capacity and completion remain Unknown.

findings.summary: Null and empty public-source results need stronger protection against zero/safe interpretation.
findings.evidence: District heat and public charging are 0/19 usable; the NBNL sample has null capacity fields alongside zeros; 50/60 water-asset capacities are null; Waterinfo T+72 is empty; weather/warning/seismic/government-service/NDW assignments are zero. These mean suppressed, unsupported, not sampled or NoData—not no assets, zero capacity, normal weather, open roads, no warning need or restored service.
findings.action: Retain typed Unknown, suppressed, not-applicable and NoData with publisher, version, retrieval, issue/valid/expiry time, coverage, licence, quality and affectsSimulation. Add regression tests preventing empty/null results from generating zero hazard, safety, passability, service or future recovery.

findings.summary: Storm, heat, winter, wildfire/smoke, cyber, earthquake and dangerous-substance events are scenario families, not calibrated Maassluis forecasts.
findings.evidence: The matrix is bounded, but there is no selected local KNMI field, ignition/perimeter, smoke plume, cyber target/architecture or seismic event/grid. Canonical wildfire has zero local flame and PM2.5 2.6 at one current DCMR station is only an indicative historical hour. The current municipal crisis page documents dangerous-substance production/storage/transport context, which is outside the ten presets.
findings.action: Require a selected versioned event/target and relevant local surface before operational claims, retain observation/forecast/scenario distinctions and disclose hazardous-material/industrial incidents as omitted rather than silently mapping them onto another preset.

findings.summary: The deterministic ten-scenario contract, arithmetic, reconciliation and selected-layer invariance pass for GM0556.
findings.evidence: The focused gate passes two tests over every required preset, checkpoint and service. Zero-intensity outputs close exactly; all local populations and service demand/delivery totals reconcile within floating-point tolerance; repeated frames are deterministic; selected-layer hazard delta is zero; cumulative event-attributable person-hours are monotonic and the zero-edge route bounds hold.
findings.action: Retain these regressions while correcting water/defence semantics, transport isolation, shared spatial allocation, lifeline evidence, forecast horizon and action/NoData gaps. Passing arithmetic is not local calibration.

corrections.summary: Replace independent generic river/coastal depth claims with an evidence-bound Nieuwe Waterweg compound boundary and defence-aware local depth model.
corrections.validation: A selected GM0556 event retains tide/surge/river components, station/datum, Maeslantkering/local-keersluis/defence state, unembanked/embanked scope, surface elevation, derived local depth, footprint, arrival/recession, issue/valid time, uncertainty, licence and NoData. Without these, exact river/coastal metres are withheld. Test that NAP water level is never labelled flood depth and that current Waterinfo stops visibly at T+48 when T+72 is absent.

corrections.summary: Repair zero-edge Maassluis transport and external-care continuity with typed modal and valid-time state.
corrections.validation: GM0556 no longer has degree zero: audited A20/local-road and appropriate metro/ferry/logistics/care dependencies carry source, authority, mode, direction, topology semantics and non-additive capacity. residualLimitations: This is a deterministic first-72-hour planning-model audit, not a Rijkswaterstaat, WMCN, Maassluis, Delfland, Veiligheidsregio Rotterdam-Rijnmond, KNMI, RIVM, DCMR or infrastructure-operator forecast, warning, probability, closure decision, evacuation order, casualty estimate or restoration commitment.

The 2025 generalized CBS boundary and neighbourhoods support overview aggregation, not parcel hydraulics, outer/inner harbour separation, defence reaches, sewer/polder catchments, asset ownership, incident perimeters or emergency routes.

No selected Nieuwe Waterweg tide, surge and river-discharge boundary, station/datum, Maeslant/local-keersluis state, defence condition, connected footprint, terrain transform, arrival/recession or uncertainty drives GM0556.
Official NAP water elevation and simulated local floodDepthM are distinct quantities. Neither the municipal phase table nor Waterinfo values directly validate modeled depth.

The municipal action plan is v1.1 May 2021 although still linked from a page modified April 2026; roles, contacts, resources and trigger operations require current municipal authorization before live use.

The public high-water map is indicative, says nothing about probability and may differ through wind, waves and backwater. Machine-service coverage, date, units, datum and NoData for GM0556 require review.
Waterinfo provides one point observation and rolling forecasts only through T+48 in the snapshot. A point is not an inundation surface or defence state; missing T+72 is NoData rather than zero.
HWH water assets have partial contributor coverage and mostly null capacities. Geometry/status labels do not establish hydraulic connectivity, setpoint, telemetry, backup or restoration.
Active Kortebuurt work and planned controls do not establish completion, event-time condition, closure or protection; sensitive inspection/operation details were not inferred.

No complete public safe source provides Stedin electricity/gas topology, Evides drinking-water pressure/quality topology, municipal sewer network, Delfland live control logic, telecom backhaul, facility dependencies, food/fuel stock, backup endurance, crews or restoration.
GM0556 currently has zero logical graph links, so no intermunicipal mobility, logistics, care or utility transfer is modeled even though A20 and transit context exist.

NWB, ProRail and GTFS are static geometry/schedule context; NDW is a current Dutch situation feed. None establishes event-time passability, metro/ferry operation, evacuation throughput or future T+72 state.
RIVM hospital roles and straight-line distances do not establish ambulance time, reachability, acceptance, staffing, occupancy, diversion, generator/fuel or backup endurance.
RDI sites do not establish operator, coverage, traffic, backhaul, backup, congestion or restoration. DUO locations do not establish shelter, reception, transport or distribution roles.
One indicative DCMR hourly PM2.5 value is not a smoke plume, population exposure, source attribution or forecast. No local wildfire perimeter/fuel/spread model is calibrated.

Cyber has no named target/architecture/attack path; earthquake has no selected event/ground-motion/site-response surface; industrial/hazardous-material incidents documented as regional context lie outside the ten presets.

Household preparedness, medically dependent people, harbour workers, visitors, mutual aid, school/institutional transport, water/reception points, medicine, food/fuel, staff, vehicles and repair priorities remain assumptions or Unknown. Seventy-two hours is preparedness scope, not a recovery deadline.

Affected population is a current post-network people-equivalent threshold metric, while deprived person-hours is a cumulative local pre-network matched-baseline service-pressure proxy. Neither is identified customers, casualties, displacement, welfare loss or economic damage; six-hour checkpoints can miss tidal peaks and rapid closures.
